tiles.visual_brief: Khan Tengri is a steep marble pyramid above the Inylchek glaciers. Classic views show its snowy southern pyramid or darker, ribbed north face glowing gold at sunset. Distinguish it from nearby Chapaev, which can appear taller from northern viewpoints, and the broader Pobeda massif.
tiles.notes: Six distinct photographs downloaded and visually checked. Prefer c1 or c2. All meet the 1600-pixel long-side minimum; five exceed 2400 pixels. Reference image untouched.

tiles.visual_brief: Aconcagua is a broad, double-summited massif with horizontal rock bands, hanging glaciers and a huge south wall above dry Andean valleys. Classic views look up Horcones valley toward the snowy south face; aerial views reveal its full bulk, while western views expose more rock. Avoid confusing neighbouring Cerro Cuerno, Catedral or Bonete with Aconcagua.
tiles.notes: Six distinct photographs downloaded and visually checked; all exceed 2400 pixels on the long side. Prefer c1 for the classic view or c2 for an aerial alternative. Wrong-subject and obscured-summit candidates were discarded.
